## 1. Installation

Install R and the compiler toolchain for your platform (Rtools on Windows,
Xcode command-line tools on macOS, or the relevant compiler and development
libraries on Linux). The sf dependency may require GDAL, GEOS and PROJ.
Install the current package:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RafaelSdeSouza/capivara", upgrade="never")
library(capivara)
packageVersion("capivara")
```

For this development tutorial before merge, install the tutorial branch
explicitly by appending @docs/reproducible-atlas-examples to the GitHub
repository name in the command above. SpectroPath is currently a package
dependency; torch and the pPXF companion are not needed for the starter.

## 2. Run your first example

No FITS download is necessary. From R:

```{r demo, eval=FALSE}
script <- system.file("tutorials", "run_prepared_cube.R",
                      package="capivara", mustWork=TRUE)
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        shQuote(c(script, "--demo", "capivara_demo", "8")))
```

Choose a new output directory on every run. The demo uses synthetic data.
For the earlier published workflow, see [Get Started](getting-started.html).

## 3. Prepare your observations

Inspect the FITS extensions, units, native wavelength coordinates, mask
bit definitions, variance, spatial orientation and instrument resolution.
Do not assume that all FITS files have the same extension or axis order.
For MUSE, CALIFA and SAMI, use a verified instrument-specific reader before
creating the following R list. Flux and variance must share the native grid.

```{r input, eval=FALSE}
# Replace these variables with data read from your instrument.
# flux, variance, good_voxels: [spatial1, spatial2, wavelength]
# host_mask: logical [spatial1, spatial2], verified source footprint
# wavelength: increasing native wavelengths in Angstrom
prepared <- list(
  flux = flux,
  variance = variance,
  valid = good_voxels,
  host_mask = host_mask,
  wavelength = wavelength,
  wavelength_frame = "observed",  # or "rest", as appropriate
  wavelength_medium = "vacuum",   # or "air", as appropriate
  flux_unit = flux_unit,
  redshift = systemic_redshift,
  object_id = object_id,
  provenance = list(source = source_file, instrument = instrument)
)
saveRDS(prepared, "my_galaxy.rds")
```

Variance is not inverse variance. Convert only finite positive IVAR values;
invalid voxels remain ineligible. Never replace missing samples with zeros.
The host mask is an explicit astronomical selection, not simply the IFU
footprint. Record how it was constructed and verify the spatial axes.

For native MaNGA DR17 LOGCUBEs, a starter adapter is included:

```{r manga, eval=FALSE}
adapter <- system.file("tutorials", "prepare_manga_cube.R",
                       package="capivara", mustWork=TRUE)
# host_mask.rds must contain your verified native-grid logical host mask.
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
  shQuote(c(adapter, "manga-8602-12705-LOGCUBE.fits.gz",
            "host_mask.rds", as.character(systemic_redshift),
            "8602-12705", "my_galaxy.rds")))
```

The adapter checks named HDUs against the expected native DRP layout.
It does not infer galaxy membership or perform LSF matching.

## 4. Analyse your own cube

```{r run, eval=FALSE}
system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        shQuote(c(script, "my_galaxy.rds", "my_galaxy_analysis", "12")))
```

Alternatively, run the analysis interactively with the existing public API:

```{r interactive, eval=FALSE}
d <- readRDS("my_galaxy.rds")
valid <- d$valid & is.finite(d$flux) &
         is.finite(d$variance) & d$variance > 0
for (j in seq_along(d$wavelength))
  valid[,,j] <- valid[,,j] & d$host_mask
cube <- list(imDat=d$flux, wavelength=d$wavelength,
             wavelength_frame=d$wavelength_frame,
             wavelength_medium=d$wavelength_medium)
seg <- segment_large(cube, Ncomp=12L, redshift=d$redshift,
                     var_cube=d$variance, sample_validity=valid,
                     representation=full_flux_representation())
quality_seg <- seg
quality_seg$original_cube$imDat[!valid] <- NA_real_
spectra <- summarize_cluster_spectra(quality_seg, var_cube=d$variance)
```

Full flux retains amplitude and shape; it is distinct from the historical
median-centred workflow. See [Semantic Representations](semantic-representations.html)
for the validated MaNGA shape profile and its limited domain. Fixed K is an
exploratory cut, not the number of physical populations. Inspect actual K,
coverage, and hierarchy QC. For large MUSE mosaics, begin with a scientifically
motivated crop; the starter materializes arrays in memory and has not been
benchmarked on full mosaics.

## 5. Understand your outputs

The starter exports a native label matrix, segmentation figure, regional
spectra CSV, region sizes, RDS segmentation object, provenance and session
information. It records finite raw sums, quality-valid sums and fixed-aperture
sums separately, including the contributing spaxel count per wavelength.
Diagonal variance is not a calibrated covariance-aware uncertainty.
The figure uses native pixel coordinates; verify celestial WCS independently
before exporting spatial products. See [FITS and DS9](fits-ds9-export.html).

## 6. Continue to physical analysis

[Kinematic Analysis](kinematic-analysis.html) documents the existing
single-line preview workflow. The optional capivaraPPXF companion provides
experimental stellar/gas fitting; consult its licence and scientific QC
before use. No calibrated physical fits, anomaly scores or semantic
classifications are produced by the starter. Unified multi-line fitting,
the interactive atlas and cross-survey validation are under development.

See [observational examples](examples.html) and the
[GitHub gallery](https://github.com/RafaelSdeSouza/capivara/tree/docs/reproducible-atlas-examples/examples)
for data access and readiness by target.

## Development validation status

This tutorial was reviewed against the current public API. The new R scripts
and FITS adapter require execution in a configured R environment; no new
observational validation is claimed by this documentation.
